thread:
maria: noticed a ~18% drop in prefix cache hit-rate for rdx-large starting 4280999800 (after the kernel selector deploy). dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/influx/d/prefix-cache/hit-rate?orgId=1

maria: per-model panel shows rdx-large down from 72% -> 54% over ~2h, per-route shows heavy impact on /chat/completions and /stream. token-saved fell ~32k tokens/hr for acme-corp slice.

aj: ack. did kernel-selector change roll out yesterday? i saw a canary that prefers new attention kernel for seq_len>1024. runtime-bot said canary started 4280999000. :eyes:

runtime-bot: deploy/canary/kernel-selector v3.4 -> started 4280999000, 12% traffic, staged autoscales enabled (no rollback).

noah: possible causes: kernel change altered runtime scheduling causing different batching shapes, or key normalization for KV cache got regressed by the same patch. any profiling?

maria: i pulled a pprof from an impacted node (canary host). CPU profile shows higher time in kv_key_digest and in kernel_dispatch. attaching snippet of the hot stack: \n\n```
pprof top -cum 30s
  18.2%  kv_key_digest
  12.7%  kernel_dispatch::select_kernel
  10.4%  batching::assemble_batch
  8.9%   attention::quantized_launch
```

aj: that kv_key_digest line worries me. did we change key hashing salt or normalization in the same PR? i remember a small refactor.

maria: checking PR 5524 — there was a canonicalization tweak for whitespace handling in prompt hashing. it should be no-op, but tests passed. maybe a path-sensitive edge.

noah: if key normalization changed, older cached prefixes won't match, explaining hit drop. but why kernel_dispatch shows up? could be more fragmented microbatches -> more kernel selection overhead. both effects compound.

aj: quick checks we can run:
- query per-tenant unique key churn: `increase(prefix_cache.keys_added[1h]) / avg(prefix_cache.key_count)`
- compare key fingerprint distribution before/after (hash prefixes modulo 256)
- sample a few requests from acme-corp that used to hit and now miss to diff the canonicalized strings

maria: ran the churn query, acme-corp keys_added spiked 3x at 4280999200 and stayed high. hash distribution shows new cluster of values not present before.

noah: ok that's consistent with normalization change. mitigation options: revert PR, or add fallback matching layer for N minutes that does both old and new normalization (costly but temporary). also we can adjust warmup: force seeded prefix keys for top 50 tenants to rebuild fast.

aj: for observability, we should add a panel that diffs "hit-rate by normalized_key_version" (v1 vs v2) and an annotation layer for kernel-selector canary windows. suggested dashboard queries:

```
# per-model per-normalization-version hit rate
sum by(model, norm_ver)(rate(prefix_cache.hit{norm_ver=~"v1|v2"}[5m])) / sum by(model, norm_ver)(rate(prefix_cache.request{norm_ver=~"v1|v2"}[5m]))

# token-saved delta per-tenant
sum by(tenant)(increase(prefix_cache.tokens_saved[1h])) - sum by(tenant)(increase(prefix_cache.tokens_saved{start<4280999000}[1h]))
```

maria: i'm going to: 1) add the dashboard panels (per-model+norm_ver, per-route heatmap, top-20 tenant token-loss), 2) open a rollback PR for the normalization change, 3) run a backfill seeded warmup for top tenants.

noah: +1 on rollback if we can do it fast. do the seeded warmup with `prefetch-seeder --tenants acme-corp,... --keys-file top_keys.csv` and throttle to avoid destabilizing kernel canaries.

aj: i'll instrument an extra metric `kernel_dispatch.overhead_ms` and add an alert if it increases >30% from baseline for a rolling 15m. also will run a microbench to measure kernel selection cost pre/post v3.4.

maria: created quick ticket RW-8342 (rollback candidate) and dashboard PR #1010. posting the sample miss diffs here: https://paste.redwood/s/maria/prefix-miss-diff.txt

noah: thanks — one more ask: add a dashboard panel that shows "warmup coverage" (percent of top-n routes whose seeded keys exist in KV) by tenant. that helps us prioritize warmups.

maria: added to PR. will post results after rollback or warmup. :thumbsup:
